feed.title: Paper Skyline devlog
feed.subtitle: What's new in each version of Paper Skyline.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 2.0.1
entry.content:
The Story of the Melancholy Melody

The Unfinished Song is now The Story of the Melancholy Melody, with a story card, a Finale card and an Events book.

Chat with residents

Chat with residents you have met from the city card.

Missions in three tabs

Missions has Main Quests, Daily and Sign-in tabs. Tap a row to act.

A new app icon and logo

Paper Skyline has a new app icon and logo, and Back in the Workshop returns to your flight.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 2.0.0
entry.content:
Three Stages in every city

Every city now has three Stages, each with tougher keepers. Your Easy, Medium and Hard clears count as Stage 1 done.

Émile, Imani and Hana

Meet Émile in Paris, Imani in New York and Hana in Tokyo. Their quests open Stages 2 and 3 and change their cities.

The Unfinished Song

Play The Unfinished Song across Paris and New York.

Menus as notebook pages

Menus are notebook pages. The Chapter page paints each city as you go, and Missions lists tasks for every city.

Relics from quests

Relics now come from quests, and the globe shows how ready your plane is for each city.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.9.6
entry.content:
A head start for new pilots

New pilots start with a $20 bonus, enough for a first upgrade after one flight.

Choose your language

New installs start in English; choose your language any time in Settings or with the flag on the title screen. Indonesian text fixes too.

A $20 bonus for new pilots

New pilots start with a $20 bonus, enough for a first upgrade after one flight.

English first, your language in Settings

New installs start in English. Choose your language any time in Settings or with the flag on the title screen.

Indonesian text fixes

Fixes for Indonesian text.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.9.5
entry.content:
Five new cities

Five new cities join the campaign. In Berlin, the Traffic-Light Man checks his pocket watch.

Terraced streets

Nine cities get new terraced streets, row on row of shopfronts.

Sharper look previews

Plane look previews stay sharp, rewarded ads no longer crash the game on some phones, and Indonesian and Chinese text fits its cards.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.9.3
entry.content:
Bahasa Indonesia

The whole game now speaks Indonesian. Pick it in Settings, under Language.

A big prize plane on Day 7

Day 7 shows a large prize plane and names its rarity.

A new Workshop layout

Looks and relics sit together in a new Workshop layout.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.9.2
entry.content:
Four new missions

Daily missions now ask you to get people to notice you, hit a top speed, fly clean without a bump, or catch coins in a row.

No ad on the landed card

A cleared city or a medal no longer shows an ad on its card.

The landed plane sits behind the walkers

After landing, the plane is drawn behind people on the street, with its trail underneath.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.9.1
entry.content:
Day 7 can be claimed again

The Day 7 card on the Daily gifts board has its Take button back, so the seventh stamp claims its gift and a new board begins.

Rockets stay in place in a dive

In a nose-down roll, the plane's rockets no longer show as a flat copy over the top of the plane.

Your colour on the Dragon and the Gyro

The Paper Dragon and the Paper Gyro now fly in the colour shown in the Garage.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.9.0
entry.content:
A Paper Pop look

The title screen, the Workshop, the landing card, the Gifts page and the Daily gifts board wear a bright new Paper Pop look: sticker buttons, round icons and a city chip on Continue.

Gifts open in colour

Opening a gift fills the room with its tier's colour. Each tap can raise the tier, and a Rich gift bursts with RICH!

Boss fights hit harder

Weak-point strikes on a Boss land with BONK!, and the final strike freezes, bursts and ends with KO! and a dizzy keeper.

Keepers introduce themselves

The first time you enter an arena, its Elite or Boss introduces itself on a torn notebook page with its name and a short story.

Missions on one screen

Missions and Gifts fit on one screen. Accept missions before a flight, and open a finished mission's gift right from the landed card.

Open one, or stop

Each kind of gift on the Gifts page has its own Open 1. Taking them all opens them in turn, and Stop keeps the rest for later.

Prices on every part

Each Workshop part shows the price of its next step, and a red dot marks the ones you can buy now. The Workshop button before a throw carries the dot too.

What the flight earned

After landing, each row's pay hops into a This flight earned callout, then into your wallet. Bars show your best for the visit.

Only the city you fly to downloads

Choosing a city downloads that city alone, so it arrives sooner. Other cities wait until you choose them.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.8.6
entry.content:
Records clear of their bars

On tablets, the landed card's records, like best here and NEW BEST, no longer overlap their bars.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.8.5
entry.content:
First missions

Four first missions lead you to your first relics: hit a keeper in Paris, break the Neko, bring home the Koban and wear it, each for a box. Treasures now drop by chance, certain by the third break.

Wind up high

From Beijing on, a headwind blows above 60 m and reaches full strength at 140 m. Gusts and the odd leaf drift past, and an arrow by the dials shows its strength. Fly lower to keep your speed and fuel.

Sharper planes

The plane in the Garage flies a slow figure-eight, smaller and sharper, and follows every look you try, Ink included. Dressed planes look sharper in flight too.

Colours on Carbon

Carbon paper takes a Colour, in a deep shade that shows on the dark paper.

Tidier numbers and fixes

Effects read compact, such as +2s fuel. The looks grid keeps its place when you tap a tile, the reward line after landing wraps instead of being cut, and translations read better.

Coloured difficulty

Easy, Medium and Hard each have their own colour, green, amber and red, on the map, the city pages and the flight picker.

A new city-clear card

Clearing a city now shows a paper card like the landing one: what the flight earned, the reward, and one button to choose the next wish or open the Workshop.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.8.4
entry.content:
Five new cities

Fly over Istanbul, Hong Kong, Toronto, Bangkok and Barcelona. Each has its own landmark, streets, Elites and Boss, and downloads once.

Looks, Relics and Properties

The Garage opens on Looks, Relics and Properties. Properties shows your plane's stats at the start of a flight and at their best, the coin pickup radius, relic slots and every worn relic effect.

Relics you can grow

Beat a keeper again on Medium or Hard for a chance at another copy of its relic, then merge copies on the Garage bench to raise its level. Each relic shows its effect as a number.

Records in the Atlas

A Records page in the Atlas gathers your career totals and every city's best flight and medals, and each city page shows its medals.

Richer trails

Soft Rain falls as slanted rain, Confetti sheds flipping pieces and Fine Sand streams loose grains.

Patterned paper fits

Patterned paper lines up across the wings and fins, and shows its pattern in the Garage while it rolls.

Garage crash fixed

Trying on one patterned paper after another in the Garage no longer runs the phone out of memory and closes the game.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.7.4
entry.content:
Continue a city you left

Choosing New flight on the title no longer loses the run you were on: that city keeps its coins and parts, and its Atlas page and the globe offer Continue.

No ink

The Ink slot gains No ink, owned from the start, for a plane without ink lines. The default paper now reads Plain paper (default).

Ten wishes at the end

The end of the tour now counts ten wishes and ten cities.

Event titles that fit

A long event title on the title screen shrinks to fit before it is shortened, so Japanese titles read in full.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.7.3
entry.content:
Smaller, livelier trails

Trail pieces are smaller now. They tumble, drift and flutter behind your plane, then fade.

$15 and $20 coins

Coins can now be worth $8, $10, $15 or $20, and Lucky coins pay $15 or $20.

Text that fits

Japanese, Korean and Chinese text fits better: the title's Atlas row, Atlas cards and keeper names in the arena.

A gift in every language

The founder gift's banner now reads in every language the game speaks.

Accept and Take

Missions in Gifts start counting when you tap Accept, and a finished one pays its box when you tap Take. A finished mission stays ready to take after the daily or weekly reset.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.7.2
entry.content:
The Garage

Open the Garage from the title screen. It holds your two relics and every look for your plane: style, paper, color, ink, fold and trail.

The Workshop

The page between flights is now called the Workshop. Upgrades stay there, and a button takes you to the Garage.

Plainer words

The game's text is rewritten in a plainer voice, in every language. You get past each city's keepers now.

A flag for every language

Every language in the menu shows its flag.

Steady streets up high

Cars, bikes and carts now come and go beyond the edges of the screen, even when you fly high.

$8 and $10 coins

Coins are worth $8 or $10 in every city, and Lucky coins are $10.

Every strike shows

Each strike that lands on an Elite or Boss shows at once: its strike count drops and the keeper reacts.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.7.1
entry.content:
Calmer streets

Fewer cars, bikes and carts share the road, so every street feels relaxed and still full of life.

Roll into every turn

Your plane now banks visibly as you steer, rolling into each climb and dive.

Trails in flight

Trail cosmetics now draw behind your plane while you fly.

Something new is waiting

Gifts and Events shimmer with a rainbow edge when there is something new to open.

Exit under Atlas

Exit now sits in the menu just below Atlas.

City treasures

Relics are now treasures, each one found in its own city.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.7.0
entry.content:
Busy streets

Cars, bikes, carts and tuk-tuks roll along the streets, each city with its own.

A plane that banks

Your plane now rolls into its turns as you climb and dive.

New sounds

Softer, musical sound effects that play in tune with each city's music.

A home for your gifts

Open Gifts from the title screen: your boxes wait there with today's missions. Tap a box three times to open it.

Daily stamps in Events

The daily stamp card now lives in Events: a gift box a day, and a Rare box on days 4 and 7.

The dragon takes wing

The red Paper Dragon is bigger and flaps its wings. It is a limited gift, while it lasts.

Cities download fresh

After this update, each city downloads once more the first time you visit it. Wi-Fi is best.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.6.3
entry.content:
A gift box every day

Daily stamps now give a gift box each day, with a Rare box on days 4 and 7. The optional ad adds a second box.

Your looks

The Looks tab shows the looks you own.

Cairo holds steady

Cairo's pyramid stays in place as you dive.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.6.2
entry.content:
Looks for your plane

Dress your plane in papers, colours, inks, folds, trails and decals, earned from flights, boxes and city clears.

Gifts and missions

Open gift boxes, fill a 7-day stamp card and take on three missions a day. Missions pay boxes, never coins.

A gift for our first flyers

Open Events and claim a red Paper Dragon, free, until 31 December 2026.

Bigger ad bonus

Watching an ad after a flight now pays at least $20.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.6.1
entry.content:
Smoother flying

Flights run at a steadier frame rate, with fewer hitches.

A cooler dawn

Morning light is softer and cooler, like an early start over the rooftops.

The spire in its place

The spire over Paris sits where it belongs again.

The nose follows the glide

As your plane glides down, its nose tips to follow the descent.

Walkers watch you fly

People in the street turn to watch your plane, stop to chat, and three new walkers join them.

Keepers fall

When you break a keeper, it now gets knocked down.

Solid skylines

Distant landmarks and bridges stay solid, softened by haze instead of fading.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.6.0
entry.content:
A gentler glide

Let go and your plane now drifts down slowly at a calm angle, then lifts its nose just before the ground.

A song for every city

Every city has its own music now, from an accordion café in Paris to jazz under the Golden Gate. Each track plays all the way through.

One calm level

City themes and the menu music now play at the same gentle volume.

Smoother skylines

The far skylines behind Rio de Janeiro and London scroll smoothly again.

Morning to evening everywhere

Like Paris, nine more cities now pass from morning light to evening as you fly.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.5.2
entry.content:
Language at a glance

The title and Settings now show your language as a flag. Tap it to pick another.

An Exit button

On Android, Exit now sits on the title and in Settings.

Walkers in front of the stand

At the start of a flight, passers-by now walk in front of the launch stand, not behind it.

Cleaner walkers

The people walking by no longer have a white outline.

The Eiffel Tower at night

The Eiffel Tower glows properly after dark, in two tones of gold.

Your language from the start

On a Vietnamese phone, Paper Skyline now opens in Vietnamese. You can still change it in Settings.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.5.1
entry.content:
Tiếng Việt

Paper Skyline now speaks Vietnamese, story and all. Pick Tiếng Việt in Settings.

Paris through the day

Fly Paris again and again and the light changes with the time of day.

A new Paris street

Paris has a new street to fly over, with fresh pavement and a new road.

People out walking

Paris's passers-by now walk with swinging arms, and a father and daughter have joined them.

The carousel horse gallops

The carousel horse now gallops when it wakes.

Smoother keepers

The keepers' idle animations are smoother.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.5.0
entry.content:
A new home screen

The game now opens at the window: the city outside, the wordmark in the sky and your plane ready to throw.

The streets notice you

People on the pavement look up when your plane flies low, and react where it lands. Paris also has a horse-drawn calèche.

Trees in the wind

Street trees now sway in passing gusts, and Paris has eleven new kinds of trees.

Keepers that move

Every keeper now moves while it waits for your plane, from the carousel horse to the kabuki actor.

No more skimming

Planes no longer skim along the rooftops. If you bought the Skim part, its coins came back to you.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.4.3
entry.content:
Replays keep your journey

Replaying an earlier city no longer moves your journey back to it. Continue always takes you to the newest city.

Continue from the Atlas

The city you are working on now has a Continue button on its Atlas page, and the globe stays on it.

Progress moves with your phone

On Android, your progress now goes into your phone's own backup, so a new phone can pick up where you left off.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.4.2
entry.content:
Every landing finishes

On some phones a flight could keep sliding forward and never end. Every landing now finishes.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.4.1
entry.content:
A friendlier first flight

Your first throw shows a ghost hand to follow. The results card says how much more your next upgrade needs, and Throw again is one tap away.

Change your mind before the throw

Before you throw, you can go back to the garage or the menu. It doesn't use up a flight.

Easier to read

The tips and buttons on the results card are bigger.

Streets that sit right

Cairo, Sydney and Rio's front rows stand on their quays, London's and Rome's landmarks are back, the clouds have soft bases and the Golden Gate is fixed.

A sidewalk for the taxi chase

The taxi fight's road now has a sidewalk on each side.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.4.0
entry.content:
Painted streets

London, Sydney, Beijing and Rome get streets painted like Paris: quays, rails, trees and pavements. And after Rio, all ten cities are yours to fly, San Francisco included.

Swipe and tap the taxi

In the taxi fight, swipe left or right to change lanes and tap anywhere to strike. No more buttons to aim for.

Every city keeps its run

Each city you've cleared keeps its own replay run: its wallet, upgrades and keepers stay where you left them.

A new skyline every flight

The buildings behind you rearrange on every flight, so no two tries look the same. The landmark, the keepers and the coins stay put.

Friendly tips

After your first flights, a short tip on the results card shows one thing to try next.

A flight cut short still pays

If your phone closes the game mid-flight, that flight now pays for how far it got when you come back.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.3.0
entry.content:
Tokyo, painted

Little houses along a stone-wall promenade, utility poles and their wires, and Fuji and the Skytree far off in the haze.

Cairo, painted

Sandstone houses by the Nile, with the Cairo Tower and the pyramids far off in the glow.

Rio, painted

Bright colonial houses on the wave pavement by the sea, with Sugarloaf rising over the bay.

A painted East River

New York's river is now painted water under the sunset.

Falling leaves in Paris

Painted plane-tree leaves tumble down as you fly over Paris.

A clock on Hard

On Hard, Elite and Boss fights run against a clock. On Easy and Medium a fight lasts until you break the keeper or run out of strikes.

The Stryge breathes

Paris's Boss now breathes slowly while it waits for you.

Garage tabs

The garage has tabs: Plane for upgrades, Relics to wear what your keepers left behind, and Records for your best flights and career.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.2.0
entry.content:
Paris, painted anew

Soft haze over the rooftops, the Seine and its bridges, and a quiet quay to glide along.

New York at sunset

Brownstones by the East River, autumn leaves, and the Empire State and Chrysler far off in the glow.

Clouds that billow

The clouds now billow as they drift by.

Hand-painted coins

Every coin along your way is now painted by hand.

The taxi's avenue

On a New York avenue, a yellow taxi keeper waits for a steady pilot. Turn your phone upright to meet it.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.1.0
entry.content:
Fly it again

Replay a city you've cleared with the plane you have now, and look for the treasures you missed.

Hard mode

A tougher way to fly each city: tighter arenas, and every keeper opens with an attack. A Hard clear earns a starred trophy.

A painted plane

Your plane is now painted by hand, and it changes as you upgrade: longer wings, taped and balsa-braced paper, a cardboard engine and its tank.

Treasures in the streets

Treasures now sit where they belong: on a painter's easel, an opera balcony, a subway step, a kite and a cable-car pylon.

The winged Sphinx

Cairo's Boss wakes up as a winged lion in black and gold. Watch its wings before you strike.

entry.title: Paper Skyline 1.0.0
entry.content:
Five cities to fly

Fly your paper plane over Paris, New York, Tokyo, Cairo and Rio de Janeiro. Each new city downloads once, then plays offline.

The keepers

Two keepers stand between you and each city's wish. Fly into their arena, switch lanes and strike when a weak point glints.

Draw a better plane

Spend what each flight earns in the garage: a stronger launcher, wider wings, tougher paper, an engine and a tank.

Hidden treasures

Rare finds hide in every city's streets. The Atlas gives you a riddle for each one you haven't found yet.

Easy or Medium

Pick how you want to fly on each city's card, before you throw.
